IF I F*CKING LOST MY IPHONE TOMORROW, I’D LOSE MY MONEY, MY EMAIL, MY TEXTS AND 11 YEARS OF PHOTOS.

GROK BOT FIXED ALL OF IT. MY PART TOOK 3 MINUTES.

I never checked how much of my life sits on one phone. Turns out: all of it.

I gave Grok Bot one job: find everything I’d lose if my iPhone disappeared tonight.

What it found:

→ Money: my bank, PayPal and my crypto exchange all log in with a text code and nothing else.
→ Email: my main inbox was SMS-only too, and it’s the reset address for 92 other accounts.
→ Photos and texts: my last iCloud backup was 7 months ago. Storage full. The warning emails were sitting unread in my inbox.
→ 38 accounts total. Zero backup codes saved anywhere.

One chain: lose the phone → lose the code → lose the email → lose everything that resets through it.

What it did:

→ Moved 31 accounts to passkeys that sync to my other devices.
→ Saved backup codes for all 38 in my password manager.
→ Flagged the full iCloud. One tap to upgrade, backups run again.
→ Set a number transfer PIN with my carrier, so nobody can move my number to their SIM.
→ Wrote one “lost phone” doc: how to lock it in Find My, freeze my cards, and get back into the 7 accounts that only support SMS.

My part: approving logins and one tap on iCloud. 3 minutes. The bot did the rest in the background.

Then I did the test. Phone in a drawer for 24 hours. I logged into everything from my laptop.

Locked out if I lose my phone: 38 → 0.

Ask yours: “Find everything I’d lose if my phone disappeared: accounts that only use text codes, my email recovery, my iCloud backup. Move what you can to passkeys, save the backup codes, and make one lost-phone doc that explains how to lock the phone, freeze my cards and recover each account.”

My full Grok Bot setup for iPhone is in the article below ↓

no f*cking way... a 20-year-old Stanford sophomore made a 90-second cartoon that hit 14 million views, alone in his dorm with Anthropic's Fable 5.2. now he just published the whole method for free

the characters, the dance, the score, every footstep: Fable built all of it from free repos. 3 of the world's top motion studios now pay him for films like it

a studio bills $3,600 and a week for 90 seconds like that. his whole cost was one weekend and the $100 plan, 36x less

his full pipeline, step by step:

the illustrator → illustrator-mcp-server
drives Adobe Illustrator from chat with 63 tools. every character comes out as clean vectors
https://t.co/SM1ye8zJYv

the rigger → Rigby2D
puts bones into a layered drawing automatically, so arms bend and heads turn
https://t.co/b2tF1Ht9hY

the animator → AnimatedDrawings
Meta's model. makes a flat drawing walk, wave and jump
https://t.co/GaOdchU4jb

the choreographer → OpenPose
reads a phone video of a real dancer, so the characters copy every move
https://t.co/pvnv22Mav6

the background painter → Wan2.2
Alibaba's video model. paints moving campus scenes behind the characters
https://t.co/asUqy4D4WM

the motion designer → anime.js
titles, logos and transitions that snap on the beat
https://t.co/DBU5jnkOi4

the composer → AudioCraft
writes an original score from a text brief, zero license fees
https://t.co/BGV7oxaCuJ

the foley artist → MMAudio
watches every shot and adds every footstep, whoosh and door slam
https://t.co/KhWoTnlsvD

the editor → Pireel
an open-source CapCut that Fable drives over MCP, timeline and all
https://t.co/E2aHwvDkvs

one of those studios offered him $65,000 a year. he said no and now sells them the same films at $1,100 each, they still bill clients $3,600

a studio with 9 people or a kid with 9 repos: who are you hiring for your next launch?

THIS IS F*CKING DANGEROUS, I USED THE SAME PASSWORD ON 47 ACCOUNTS. ONE LEAK AND SOMEONE COULD OPEN ALL OF THEM.

GROK BOT FOUND IT AND MADE EVERY ONE UNIQUE. MY PART TOOK 4 MINUTES.

Bank, email, PayPal, X, Instagram, my crypto exchange. Same password since 2016. Just a “!” at the end on the sites that wanted a symbol.

My password manager had been flagging it for years. I never opened that tab.

Turns out hackers don’t guess passwords anymore. They take one leaked email and password and try it on hundreds of sites automatically. It’s called credential stuffing, and it takes them minutes.

I gave Grok Bot one job: find every account my old password still opens.

What it found:

→ 47 accounts with the same password, or the same one plus “!”.
→ That password was already in 2 public data breaches, from 2019 and 2022.
→ My email and my bank were both on the list.
→ 6 accounts I forgot I even had.

What it did:

→ Started with what hurts most: email, bank, PayPal, crypto.
→ Changed all 47 to unique random passwords, saved straight into my password manager.
→ Turned on passkeys wherever the site supports them.
→ Deleted the 6 accounts I didn’t need anymore.
→ Signed out every old session after each change.

My part: approving each change. 4 minutes. The bot did the rest.

One leaked password used to open 47 doors. Now it opens zero.

and most of them had no idea for two weeks

here's what happened

hackers broke into fireworks AI, a company cursor shared data with

inside they found an access key cursor had given them

they used it to dig deeper into cursor's systems and grabbed more credentials

then on october 29 they used those credentials to slip two poisoned versions of the claude code extension into cursor's marketplace

it looked like a normal update

it wasn't

it installed a persistent SSH backdoor. a secret door into your machine that survives restarts

it was live for about 11 hours before cursor caught it and pulled the marketplace offline

cursor says up to 5,000 people may have received it

the bad versions: 2.1.312 and 2.1.313

if that might be you, do this tonight:

1. open your extensions in cursor and check your claude code version history
2. check your email for a notice from cursor. they contacted affected users
3. look at ~/.ssh/authorized_keys and delete any key you don't recognize
4. rotate everything that machine touched: github tokens, API keys, cloud logins, SSH keys
5. if you're not sure, treat the machine as compromised. a clean reinstall beats guessing

and for everyone else, the lessons:

→ turn on privacy mode in your AI tools so your sessions don't get stored and shared
→ never paste passwords or API keys into AI chats or support tickets. some of the stolen credentials came from exactly that
→ use short lived tokens with the minimum access they need
→ keep real secrets in a password manager or secret vault, not in your code or chats
→ for extensions that can run code on your machine, don't auto update blindly. wait a day and watch for reports

the scary part?

you didn't have to do anything wrong

you just clicked update
